minor: All 7 children use `var(--etsl-color-*, <hex>)` fallbacks. component-conventions.md bans var() fallbacks; the deviation is deliberate so each child's standalone story renders without the root's :host palette in scope. Zero fallbacks on any --sl-* token.

sl-panel UPSTREAM DEFECT: panel.css gives [part=header] `flex: 1` and the body no grow factor on a column-flex host, so a stretched panel grows its grey HEADER, not its body. Rendered a 354px header here. Worked around with .panel::part(header){flex:0 0 auto} + ::part(body){flex:1 1 auto}.

sl-progress-bar UPSTREAM BUG: progress-bar.css:66 uses `font: var(--sl-text-new-heading-sm)`, a BARE token editorial-suite does not define (longhands only), so its label typography is dropped silently for every consumer of this theme.

editorial-suite THEME DEFECT: public --sl-text-new-typeset-fontFamily-{body,heading} resolve to 'Open Sans', which the theme's own Typekit (bws3iof) does not ship - it ships raleway + roboto. The brand tokens and the legacy --sl-heading-fontFamily/--sl-text-fontFamily are correct. Using the public tokens would render a fallback face; this run used the legacy ones.

sl-button exposes no part for its background/label, so brand colour is applied by retargeting the tokens it reads (--sl-color-background-primary-bold etc.) on individual elements - a reach-through, not a supported API.
sl-panel tightens its header inline padding only under :host([has-actions]), which it sets for slot='actions' but not the slot='aside' this run uses (OQ12); compensated in the run CSS.
sl-tab-group's selected indicator is not exposed as a ::part(), so its colour can only be changed by retargeting --sl-color-border-selected on the element.

themeMatch.note: The batch assigned editorial-suite by product name (ETSL = Editorial Suite), but the design file's colour variables agree 14/14 with sanoma-learning and only 5/14 with editorial-suite. Theme NOT switched - the runbook fixes it per run and switching would make this run incomparable. This explains why #006666/#02242E/#CA6F2A were unbound, and why #0d8e4c/#d3f8de were found only in sanoma-learning.

themeDerived.note: Captured under 'editorial-suite', assigned from the team label before themes were derived. The ETSL design file speaks sanoma-learning's vocabulary and matches it on every colour token. Colour measurements in this run therefore describe the wrong theme; geometry, DOM structure and token-name findings are unaffected. The run did not switch themes mid-flight, which was the right call — the theme is a recorded run parameter, not something to change once captures exist.
